syllabus_anchor: Animal kingdom: chordates; salient features and classification of vertebrates
reasoning_focus: A crocodilian exception prevents four heart chambers from being used as a unique class marker
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Three vertebrates are compared. P has a three-chambered heart, moist glandular skin and a larval stage with gills; Q has dry scales, a four-chambered heart and lays shelled eggs on land; R has feathers and a four-chambered heart. Which classification uses the combination of traits without treating heart-chamber number as sufficient?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: P combines the moist glandular covering and aquatic larval respiration characteristic of amphibians. Most reptiles have an incompletely divided ventricle, but crocodilians have a four-chambered heart; dry scales and shelled terrestrial eggs place Q with reptiles despite this exception. Feathers identify R as a bird. Thus the same heart-chamber count can occur in different vertebrate classes, and several independent characters must be combined.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) exchanges the amphibian and reptile coverings and ignores R's feathers. (B) assigns a featherless scaled animal to birds and a feathered animal to reptiles. (D) gills in an amphibian larva do not make the adult a fish, and Q lacks the diagnostic mammalian combination.

syllabus_anchor: Anatomy of flowering plants: epidermal tissue system; stomata and guard cells
reasoning_focus: Guard-cell specialisation and alternative stomatal geometry distinguished from ordinary epidermal cells
object_constraints_and_requested_result: The diagram compares two mature epidermal stomatal complexes. P has kidney-shaped guard cells and Q has dumbbell-shaped guard cells; the surrounding epidermal cells lack the dark chloroplast bodies shown in the guard cells. Which interpretation is supported?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Each complex consists of a pore bounded by two specialised guard cells. Kidney-shaped guard cells occur widely, whereas the dumbbell form is characteristic of grasses. Guard cells can contain chloroplasts even when the ordinary epidermal cells shown lack them. The diagram therefore compares specialisation within the epidermis rather than two different vascular tissues. It does not establish a photosynthetic function for every surrounding cell.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) incorrectly makes one common guard-cell shape universal. (C) transfers a feature of the specialised guard cells to all epidermal cells despite the observed contrast. (D) confuses a paired surface pore apparatus with an internal conducting vessel.

syllabus_anchor: Biomolecules: enzymes; factors affecting enzyme activity; substrate concentration
reasoning_focus: Saturating initial rates scale with active-site number without changing the half-maximum substrate concentration
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Two identical enzyme preparations are assayed at the same optimal pH and temperature with saturating substrate. Preparation Q contains twice as much active enzyme as P. Initial rates are measured before appreciable substrate depletion. Which pair of changes is expected for Q relative to P?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: With substrate saturating, the number of functioning catalytic sites limits the initial total rate. Q has twice as many equivalent sites, so it can process twice as much substrate per unit time. The molecular affinity and turnover properties of each enzyme molecule are unchanged under the matched conditions. Therefore the substrate concentration giving half of that preparation's own maximum remains the same. The initial-rate condition prevents later substrate depletion from obscuring this comparison.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) keeps the site-limited maximum fixed and wrongly changes the enzyme's substrate dependence. (B) reverses the effect of adding active catalytic sites. (C) confuses a vertical rate scaling with a change in the horizontal substrate-concentration scale.

syllabus_anchor: Plant growth and development: arithmetic and geometric growth; differentiation
reasoning_focus: Division competence determines arithmetic versus geometric cell-lineage growth
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A model plant cell lineage starts with one dividing cell. In lineage P each division produces one cell that keeps dividing and one cell that permanently differentiates. In lineage Q both daughters keep dividing. Cells divide once per equal interval, with no death. After four intervals, what are the total cell counts P and Q, and the corresponding growth patterns?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Count only daughters retaining division competence when determining the next interval's increase.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) omits the initial cell and undercounts Q's doubling. (C) gives P geometric proliferation contrary to permanent differentiation. (D) exchanges the two lineage rules.

syllabus_anchor: Neural control and coordination: generation and conduction of nerve impulse
reasoning_focus: An early spike can use existing ion gradients despite inhibition of their long-term pump maintenance
object_constraints_and_requested_result: An isolated axon initially has normal ion gradients. A brief treatment blocks the sodium–potassium pump but does not block voltage-gated channels. Before the gradients substantially dissipate, a threshold stimulus is applied. Which statement best separates the action potential from long-term gradient maintenance?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Rapid depolarisation normally involves increased sodium permeability through gated channels, followed by increased potassium permeability during repolarisation. These passive movements use electrochemical gradients already present before the stimulus. The sodium–potassium pump supports those gradients over longer periods but is not the gated pathway carrying each rapid spike current. The stipulated short observation interval matters: after extended inhibition, repeated activity and ion leakage would undermine the gradients and excitability.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) replaces the voltage-gated sodium pathway with the slower maintenance pump. (C) reverses the usual outward potassium movement during repolarisation and assigns it to the wrong mechanism. (D) assumes inhibition instantly removes previously established concentration differences.

syllabus_anchor: Reproductive health: contraception; sexually transmitted infections and prevention
reasoning_focus: Preventing ovulation does not supply a barrier against sexually transmitted infection
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A couple correctly uses oral contraceptive pills. They believe this also protects them from sexually transmitted infections. Which advice correctly distinguishes contraceptive action from infection prevention?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Oral contraceptives alter reproductive hormonal control and can prevent ovulation or otherwise reduce pregnancy probability. That action does not prevent contact with infectious secretions or pathogens during sexual intercourse. Correct condom use provides a barrier that reduces transmission risk as well as contributing to contraception. Risk reduction should not be described as an absolute guarantee, and neither pill use nor an intrauterine device substitutes for the relevant barrier.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) confuses blocking egg release with blocking pathogen entry. (B) incorrectly attributes universal infection protection to an intrauterine device. (D) makes a barrier's infection-prevention role depend on the ovarian cycle, although pathogen exposure does not require ovulation.

syllabus_anchor: Principles of inheritance and variation: sex determination in humans, birds and honeybees
reasoning_focus: Bird ZW, human XY and honeybee haplodiploidy differ in the variable parental contribution
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Ignore exceptional sex-determination mechanisms. A hen produces Z-bearing or W-bearing eggs; a human female produces X-bearing eggs; a queen honeybee can lay fertilised or unfertilised eggs. Which comparison is correct?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Female birds are ZW and males ZZ, so alternative eggs provide the variable sex chromosome. In humans the female is XX and the male XY, making sperm type the variable chromosomal contribution. In honeybees, ordinary unfertilised eggs develop parthenogenetically into haploid males, whereas fertilised eggs develop into diploid females. These mechanisms cannot be collapsed into one universal rule about which parent determines sex.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) wrongly applies the human XY pattern to birds and haplodiploidy. (B) ignores the human male's alternative X- and Y-bearing sperm. (C) reverses both the ploidy and the usual sex of an unfertilised honeybee egg.

syllabus_anchor: Human health and disease: allergy; autoimmunity; immunodeficiency
reasoning_focus: Controlled allergen evidence, self-antigen injury and helper-cell deficiency distinguish three immune failures
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Three patients are investigated. P develops a rapid wheal after a harmless pollen challenge; a matched test without pollen is negative and allergen-specific IgE is elevated. Q has antibodies reacting with the patient's own joint tissue and inflammatory injury. R repeatedly develops opportunistic infections and has severely reduced helper T-cell counts. Which assignment fits the targets and response evidence?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: P has an antigen-dependent excessive response to an ordinarily harmless environmental substance, consistent with an IgE-associated allergy. Q's response is directed against self tissue, which identifies loss of self tolerance rather than an exaggerated response to an external allergen. R has impaired helper T-cell availability together with infections that normally controlled immunity would resist. The matched negative challenge in P separates the observed pollen response from an unrelated skin reaction; the three cases therefore require both the target and the effectiveness of defence to be considered.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) exchanges the external and self targets and misreads reduced defence as enhancement. (C) reverses the evidence for P and R and assigns Q the wrong target class. (D) ignores the distinct self-directed response and T-cell deficit.

syllabus_anchor: Biotechnology principles and processes: methods of introducing recombinant DNA into host cells
reasoning_focus: Host barriers determine competence treatment, microinjection or biolistic DNA delivery
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Three DNA-delivery tasks are planned: P introduces DNA into chemically treated bacterial cells; Q delivers DNA directly into the nucleus of an animal cell; R delivers DNA across a plant cell wall without first making protoplasts. Which methods match these physical barriers?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Chemical competence treatment can increase bacterial DNA uptake, with the appropriate heat-shock step aiding transformation. A fine micropipette can place DNA directly into an animal-cell nucleus during microinjection. Biolistics uses DNA-coated particles to cross plant-cell barriers, including walls, and does not require every target cell to be converted into a protoplast first. Successful delivery still does not by itself prove stable integration or expression.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) swaps direct animal-cell injection with plant particle delivery and gives the intact plant the bacterial procedure. (B) invokes a bacterial nucleus, which bacteria lack, and mismatches the targets. (D) wrongly treats heat shock as precise nuclear injection and claims a gene gun removes all walls.

syllabus_anchor: Organisms and populations: population density and its alternative measures
reasoning_focus: Biomass, numerical density and percentage cover answer different population questions
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A lake contains a few very large fish and thousands of tiny plankton, while a rock face carries a spreading lichen mat whose individuals cannot be separated reliably. Which measurements best answer respectively: fish contribution to living mass, plankton abundance, and extent of lichen occupation?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Individual number can greatly understate the mass contribution of a few large organisms, so fish biomass addresses the first question directly. A standard-volume count gives a reproducible abundance measure for dispersed plankton. Percentage cover measures occupation by a lichen mat when boundaries between individuals are not operationally reliable. These measures are not interchangeable numerical units, but each can represent population presence or density for its specified purpose.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) supplies measurements that fail the mass, abundance or boundary constraints. (C) substitutes unrelated attributes for the requested quantities. (D) makes individual count universal despite the explicit difficulty of delimiting lichen individuals.

syllabus_anchor: Principles of inheritance and variation: multiple alleles; ABO blood groups; codominance
reasoning_focus: ABO offspring possibilities separate codominance within an individual from multiple alleles in a population
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Two parents with blood group AB have a child. Assume the usual ABO alleles and no rare phenotypes. Which statement correctly links the possible child phenotypes to the meaning of multiple alleles and codominance?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Each AB parent transmits either IA or IB. Their offspring can therefore be IAIA, IAIB or IBIB, producing A, AB or B phenotypes. IA and IB are both expressed in a heterozygous AB individual, which is codominance. Multiple allelism instead describes the existence of IA, IB and i in the population; one ordinary diploid individual still carries only two alleles at the locus. Neither parent in this cross carries i.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) invents an i allele absent from both parental genotypes. (B) treats codominance as permanent blending that abolishes segregation. (C) confuses the population's allele inventory with an individual's diploid genotype.

syllabus_anchor: Principles of inheritance and variation: linkage and recombination
reasoning_focus: Observed linkage strength does not uniquely determine a ratio of physical chromosome distances
object_constraints_and_requested_result: In the same species, two separate linked marker pairs P–Q and R–S give recombinant fractions of 0.10 and 0.45 in large test crosses, with no viability differences. Which inference is justified without additional physical or multi-marker data?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Fewer recombinant offspring indicate stronger observed association for P–Q under the stated equal-viability conditions. A fraction close to one-half can arise from widely separated loci on the same chromosome as well as independent assortment, so R–S need not lie on different chromosomes. Multiple exchanges can restore parental marker arrangements and go uncounted as recombinants. Therefore the two fractions cannot be converted into an exact ratio of DNA lengths using these data alone.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) invents a 0.25 boundary for different chromosomes. (C) contradicts both the linkage interpretation and the exclusion of differential survival. (D) ignores undetected multiple exchanges and variation in recombination along chromosomes.

syllabus_anchor: Body fluids and circulation: ECG; cardiac cycle; pressure-dependent valve function
reasoning_focus: ECG ventricular depolarisation precedes pressure-driven valve opening and actual ejection
object_constraints_and_requested_result: The aligned trace shows a normal ECG and left-ventricular and aortic pressures. At marker X the QRS complex has just occurred, ventricular pressure is rising above left-atrial pressure but remains below aortic pressure. At Y the ventricular pressure first exceeds aortic pressure. Which sequence is consistent with excitation and valve mechanics?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: QRS reflects ventricular depolarisation, not the volume of blood being ejected. As contraction develops, ventricular pressure closes the mitral valve once it exceeds atrial pressure. Until it also exceeds aortic pressure, the aortic valve remains closed, so the intervening contraction can occur with both valves shut and no ejection. The crossing near Y supplies the pressure condition for aortic opening and the start of ejection. This combines the ECG with the pressure evidence instead of treating them as identical events.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) confuses depolarisation with repolarisation and opens the outlet too early. (B) equates an electrical waveform with a mechanical flow event. (D) contradicts the reversed pressure difference across the mitral valve at X.

syllabus_anchor: Cell the unit of life: cilia, flagella, centrosome and centrioles
reasoning_focus: Peripheral doublets with a central pair distinguished from a nine-triplet basal-body cylinder
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Two transverse microtubule schematics are shown. P has nine peripheral doublets and a central pair; Q has nine peripheral triplets and no central pair. Which interpretation correctly relates these organisations?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: The typical motile eukaryotic ciliary or flagellar axoneme has nine peripheral microtubule doublets and two central microtubules. Centrioles and basal bodies instead have nine peripheral triplets without that central pair. Nine peripheral groups alone therefore does not make the organisations identical. Bacterial flagella have a different protein organisation and are not built as the pictured 9+2 microtubule axoneme.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) exchanges the eukaryotic structures and incorrectly assigns microtubule architecture to a bacterial flagellum. (C) ignores doublet versus triplet membership and the centre. (D) reverses the peripheral totals: nine doublets contain 18 and nine triplets 27 microtubules.

syllabus_anchor: Ecosystem: energy flow; grazing and detritus food chains
reasoning_focus: Grazing and detritus pathways share producer-derived energy without cyclic energy regeneration
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A forest's dead leaves enter a detritus food chain, while some living leaves are eaten by grazing herbivores. Which statement correctly describes the relation between the two routes and the energy source?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: A living leaf and its later litter both contain chemical energy derived from primary production. Herbivores can receive some through grazing, whereas decomposers and detritivores can receive some after material enters the detritus pathway. Transfers involve respiration and heat dissipation, so the energy flow requires continuing external input. Recycling mineral nutrients does not restore dissipated energy to its original high-quality form.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) mistakes use of stored chemical energy for creation of new energy. (B) turns nutrient cycling into complete energy recycling. (C) denies the energy available to consumers of dead organic material.

syllabus_anchor: Chemical bonding: molecular orbital theory; homonuclear diatomic molecules
reasoning_focus: C2 molecular-orbital filling separates bond order from an assumed occupied 2p sigma bond
object_constraints_and_requested_result: For ground-state C2, use the valence molecular-orbital order shown: sigma(2s), sigma*(2s), pi(2px)=pi(2py), sigma(2pz). The bond axis is z. Fill eight valence electrons according to the usual rules. Which statement follows within this MO model?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Bond order is half the excess of bonding over antibonding electrons; unpaired occupancy determines magnetism.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) stops after single occupation instead of placing all four remaining electrons. (C) misidentifies the shown pi bonding levels as antibonding. (D) places electrons in a higher empty level without enough electrons.

syllabus_anchor: Coordination compounds: ligands; denticity; coordination number; applications of EDTA
reasoning_focus: EDTA donor count and complex charge distinguished from colour and transition-metal status
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Let Y4− denote fully deprotonated EDTA with two amine nitrogen donors and four carboxylate oxygen donors binding one Ca2+ ion. A stable colourless complex forms. Which description is correct?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Denticity counts donor atoms of the same ligand attached to one metal, not merely the number of negatively charged groups. The two nitrogen donors add to the four oxygen donors, so the stated binding mode is hexadentate. Combining Ca2+ with Y4− gives a complex charge of −2. Coordination is not restricted to transition metals, and visible colour is not a necessary consequence of every metal–ligand interaction.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) ignores four donors and fails to add charges. (C) excludes neutral nitrogen lone-pair donation and undercounts denticity. (D) makes a metal-class label cancel a real ionic charge.

syllabus_anchor: The d- and f-block elements: potassium permanganate; redox reactions
reasoning_focus: Permanganate thermal decomposition couples oxygen evolution to two distinct manganese reductions
object_constraints_and_requested_result: On heating, potassium permanganate gives potassium manganate, manganese dioxide and oxygen. In the balanced equation containing two KMnO4 units, what is the coefficient of O2 and how many electrons are transferred internally from oxygen to manganese?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Balance atoms and then equate oxidation-state increases and decreases.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) doubles oxygen beyond atom balance. (B) supplies too little oxygen and too few electron equivalents. (D) confuses zero net formula charge with unchanged elemental oxidation states.

syllabus_anchor: Classification of elements and periodicity: electronic configuration; periodic chemical trends
reasoning_focus: Period-3 configurations and basic–amphoteric–acidic oxide behaviour provide independent identification cues
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Three Period-3 oxides are tested. P reacts with acid but not aqueous alkali; Q reacts with both; R reacts with alkali but not acid under the stated test conditions. The candidate parent configurations are [Ne]3s1, [Ne]3s2 3p1 and [Ne]3s2 3p2. Which assignment best fits the usual acid–base trend?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: The three configurations identify sodium, aluminium and silicon in that order. Across the period the character of their typical oxides changes from strongly basic through amphoteric to acidic as metallic character decreases. Reaction with both acid and alkali is therefore the diagnostic contrast for aluminium oxide here. The claim concerns the usual acid–base behaviour of these oxides, not an assertion that all oxides in a block share one universal behaviour.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) assigns the alkali-reactive acidic oxide to the basic observation. (B) exchanges all three behaviours. (C) makes silicon oxide amphoteric and aluminium oxide purely acidic in these tests.

syllabus_anchor: Structure of atom: Heisenberg uncertainty principle; momentum and kinetic energy
reasoning_focus: Unequal confinement and unequal mass give opposite rankings of velocity spread and kinetic-energy scale
object_constraints_and_requested_result: For a one-dimensional uncertainty comparison, an electron has position uncertainty a and a proton has position uncertainty a/1000. Take mp=1836me and use the Heisenberg lower bound at equality for both. Define the associated kinetic-energy scale as (delta p)^2/(2m). What are the proton/electron ratios of velocity uncertainty and this energy scale?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: \[\Delta x\Delta p\ge\hbar/2,\quad \Delta v=\Delta p/m,\quad K_*=(\Delta p)^2/(2m).\]
distractor_mechanisms: (A) ignores mass and momentum squaring. (C) reverses both requested ratios. (D) assumes equal momentum uncertainty despite unequal confinement.

syllabus_anchor: Some basic concepts of chemistry: mole concept; stoichiometry; mass percentage
reasoning_focus: Retained water in a gravimetric product creates a directional sample-purity bias
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A 0.500 g impure NaCl sample contains only a chloride-free inert impurity. Its chloride is completely precipitated as AgCl. The collected solid weighs 1.248 g before drying and 1.148 g after drying to constant mass; the loss is only water. Take M(AgCl)=143.5 and M(NaCl)=58.5 g mol−1. What NaCl mass percentage follows, and what error would using the wet mass cause?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Convert the dry precipitate to moles and use the one-to-one chloride stoichiometry.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) reverses the direction of the wet-mass bias. (C) assumes perfect purity without using the chloride amount. (D) fails to convert precipitate mass into NaCl mass using their different molar masses.

syllabus_anchor: Organic chemistry basic principles: resonance; reaction intermediates
reasoning_focus: Allylic-radical contributors preserve connectivity, charge and unpaired-electron number
object_constraints_and_requested_result: The diagram shows two valid resonance contributors of an allylic carbon radical, with the double bond and single unpaired electron on opposite terminal positions. What remains unchanged between the contributors?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: The three-carbon sigma framework is identical in both contributors. Moving the pi-electron and radical descriptions does not add or remove an electron, so the overall neutral charge and one unpaired electron are retained. The real allylic radical has delocalised electronic character rather than being a time average of independently isolable molecules. The drawings are bookkeeping contributors to one electronic structure.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) confuses electron redistribution with rotation of an atomic framework. (C) creates charges absent from the displayed electron counts. (D) treats resonance contributors as distinct chemical species in equilibrium.

syllabus_anchor: Hydrocarbons: alkenes; addition reactions; organic stereoisomerism
reasoning_focus: Anti addition and internal symmetry determine different stereochemical sets from cis and trans alkenes
object_constraints_and_requested_result: The figure shows cis- and trans-but-2-ene separately. Under conditions that give stereospecific anti addition of Br2, with no rearrangement or subsequent epimerisation, which product comparison is correct? Count configurational stereoisomers, including both members of a racemate.
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Each alkene carbon becomes a stereocentre after bromine addition. Adding from opposite faces to cis-but-2-ene produces the R,R and S,S pair, with equal access to the two mirror-related approaches in an achiral environment. Anti addition to trans-but-2-ene instead gives the R,S arrangement, which is identical to S,R by the molecule's internal symmetry and is meso. Thus a formal two-centre count must be filtered by both the addition constraint and molecular symmetry.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) reverses the anti-addition outcomes. (B) invents selection of a single handed product without a chiral influence. (C) ignores the meso identity and the stereospecific starting geometry.

syllabus_anchor: Haloalkanes and haloarenes: polyhalogen compounds; chloroform
reasoning_focus: Chloroform storage precautions distinguish oxidation prevention from phosgene trapping
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A chloroform sample is exposed to air and light, producing a toxic oxidation product, carbonyl chloride. A separate sample is stored in a dark, tightly stoppered bottle containing a little ethanol. Which explanation correctly assigns the roles of the precautions?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Chloroform can be oxidised by air in the presence of light to carbonyl chloride, also called phosgene. Dark storage and restricted contact with air reduce the conditions favouring that change. The added ethanol reacts with phosgene, helping remove the hazardous product rather than merely lowering its concentration by a trivial volume addition. These roles explain why the precautions are combined rather than treating one as proof that no reactive impurity can ever form.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) reverses the role of darkness and invents simple reductive dechlorination. (B) assumes stoppering instantaneously eliminates pre-existing dissolved oxygen. (D) proposes complete salt formation that is not the stated storage chemistry.

syllabus_anchor: Alcohols phenols and ethers: chemical reactions of phenols; Reimer–Tiemann and Kolbe reactions
reasoning_focus: Reimer–Tiemann formylation and Kolbe carboxylation lead to different diagnostic oxidation and acid-base responses
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Phenol is subjected to two independent preparations. Route P uses CHCl3/aqueous NaOH followed by acid work-up; route Q uses sodium phenoxide with CO2 under pressure followed by acid work-up. Considering the usual major ortho products, which pair of product groups and separate tests is correct?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Both routes add one carbon adjacent to the hydroxyl group, but reagent identity determines its oxidation state and functional group. Diagnostic tests must be applied to those actual groups rather than to carbon count or aromaticity alone.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) identifies different oxidation states as one product. (C) assigns groups formed by neither route. (D) wrongly exempts an aromatic aldehyde from the Tollens response and denies carboxylic acidity.

syllabus_anchor: Biomolecules: hormones; proteins and peptide bonds
reasoning_focus: Protease sensitivity distinguishes peptide structure from steroid structure without changing the common signalling role
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A peptide hormone and a steroid hormone are assayed separately before and after exhaustive protease treatment. The peptide hormone loses activity; the steroid hormone retains activity under the same treatment. Which conclusion is best supported?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: A peptide hormone contains a polypeptide structure whose integrity can matter for recognition and biological activity. Protease hydrolysis disrupts peptide bonds and can therefore abolish its activity. A steroid has a different carbon-ring framework rather than a peptide backbone, so the same enzyme need not destroy it. The matched treatment supports a chemical-class distinction while preserving the shared signalling role of the two hormones.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) makes all hormones proteins despite the explicitly different steroid structure. (C) infers inorganic composition from resistance to one selective enzyme. (D) confuses chemical messengers with bulk metabolic fuels and dismisses a relevant structural change.

syllabus_anchor: Equilibrium: ionic equilibrium; salt hydrolysis; amphiprotic species
reasoning_focus: Competing proton donation and acceptance explain basic bicarbonate without a universal hydrogen-salt rule
object_constraints_and_requested_result: For carbonic acid, take Ka1=5×10−7, Ka2=5×10−11 and Kw=10−14. In an aqueous NaHCO3 solution where water's own ionisation is not dominant, which comparison correctly explains the usual pH above 7?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Bicarbonate's charge does not forbid proton donation, but it can also accept a proton from water. Comparing those competing tendencies explains an alkaline rather than acidic salt solution in the stated regime. Na+ is a spectator ion for this hydrolysis.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) denies the retained acidic proton. (B) ignores the relative acid and base strengths. (D) assigns hydrolysis to the cation of a strong base.

syllabus_anchor: Solutions: solubility of gases; Henry law
reasoning_focus: Temperature-dependent Henry constant can cancel a simultaneous increase in gas partial pressure
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A dilute nonreacting gas follows p=KH x. At T1 its Henry constant is K and its mole fraction over a gas mixture is x1. At T2 the constant becomes 4K, total pressure doubles, and the gas-phase mole fraction of this gas changes from 0.20 to 0.40. What is x2/x1, and does total pressure alone predict the solubility change?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Dissolved mole fraction is partial pressure divided by the temperature-specific Henry constant.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) ignores the composition change and overstates what total pressure establishes. (C) treats KH as unchanged despite the stated factor of four. (D) omits the KH change and denies partial-pressure dependence.

syllabus_anchor: Electrochemistry: electrolysis; Faraday laws
reasoning_focus: Parallel electrolysis requires branch-specific charge rather than series-cell equality
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Two electrolytic cells operate in parallel for 9650 s. The copper cell carries a constant 0.20 A and deposits Cu from Cu2+; the silver cell carries 0.30 A and deposits Ag from Ag+. Current efficiencies are 100%. Use F=96500 C mol−1 and atomic masses Cu=63.5, Ag=108. What are the deposited masses Cu and Ag?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: \[n_e=It/F,\quad n_{\rm metal}=n_e/z.\]
distractor_mechanisms: (A) omits copper's two-electron requirement. (B) wrongly gives silver a two-electron requirement. (C) divides total charge equally despite the unequal currents.

syllabus_anchor: Thermodynamics: Gibbs energy; spontaneity; coupled processes
reasoning_focus: Stoichiometric coupling changes overall Gibbs feasibility without changing an isolated component's sign
object_constraints_and_requested_result: At a fixed temperature and composition, reaction R has delta G=+20 kJ per written reaction and S has delta G=−50 kJ per written reaction. An ideal coupling mechanism carries out exactly two R events per S event. What is delta G per coupled event, and what does it imply?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Add Gibbs changes with the actual stoichiometric coefficients of the coupled process.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) adds R only once and wrongly makes each part favourable. (B) reverses the sum and denies the role of coupling. (C) transfers the sign of the combined process to an uncoupled component.

syllabus_anchor: Coordinate geometry: circle chords; distance of a point from a line
reasoning_focus: Concentric chord-length difference fixes line distance before an external point fixes two slopes
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Two circles centred at the origin have radii 5 and sqrt(13). A line through (0,5) cuts both circles into chords whose lengths differ by 4. What is the product of the slopes of all such lines?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Chord length is twice the radius–distance right-triangle leg.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) inverts the squared slope. (B) loses the opposite signs. (D) reports one slope instead of their product.

syllabus_anchor: Conic sections: parabola; tangents; differentiation of implicit functions
reasoning_focus: Translated parabola reconstruction combines directrix, tangent slope and contact incidence
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A right-opening parabola has horizontal axis and directrix x=−1. The line y=x is tangent at (2,2). What is the focus?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Its directrix is x=h−p and its tangent slope satisfies 2(y−k)y'=4p.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) is the vertex. (B) is the contact point, not the focus. (C) lies on the directrix and reverses the focus location.

syllabus_anchor: Differentiation: logarithmic derivative; second derivatives; maxima and minima
reasoning_focus: Logarithmic differentiation and second derivative establish the global minimum of a variable-base power
object_constraints_and_requested_result: For f(x)=x^x on x>0, which statement correctly describes its stationary point and curvature?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Differentiate the logarithm, then recover the derivatives of f.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) reverses the derivative sign change and curvature. (C) includes an excluded endpoint and a nonstationary point. (D) confuses positive height with positive slope.

syllabus_anchor: Integration: properties and evaluation of definite integrals; monotonicity
reasoning_focus: Pointwise ordering proves uniqueness of a parameter in a definite integral
object_constraints_and_requested_result: For a≥0 define F(a)=the integral from 0 to 1 of 1/(1+ax) dx. How many values of a satisfy F(a)=ln 2?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Compare integrands pointwise before attempting to solve a transcendental equation.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) ignores the explicit working value. (B) contradicts strict decrease. (C) treats an integral identity at one value as an identity for every parameter.

syllabus_anchor: Relations and functions: composition; rational functions; quadratic equations
reasoning_focus: A rational three-cycle requires domain exclusions and a separate absence-of-fixed-points check
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Let f(x)=(x−1)/x. Consider real starting values for which every successive iterate is defined. Which statement about the smallest positive iterate returning to the starting value is correct?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Compose the rational map, then test smaller divisors of a returning iterate for fixed points.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) confuses a three-cycle with an involution. (C) misses a later denominator and asserts fixedness. (D) uses a starting value whose next composition is undefined.

syllabus_anchor: Matrices: elementary column operations; inverse; systems of linear equations
reasoning_focus: A column update is checked through determinant preservation and one inverse-column system
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Let A have columns c1,c2,c3 and rows (1,1,0),(0,1,1),(1,0,1). Form B with columns c1,c2+2c1,c3. What is the first column of B inverse?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: The first inverse column v solves Bv=e1; a column-addition operation preserves determinant.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) gives the opposite unit image. (C) is the original A inverse column before the change. (D) has twice the required scale.

syllabus_anchor: Probability: conditional probability; finite sample spaces; complementary events
reasoning_focus: A reported minimum conditions ordered dice triples without selecting a labelled die
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Three distinguishable fair six-sided dice are thrown. Given that the minimum of the three results is exactly 2, what is the probability that their sum is 8?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Count the reported-minimum event before counting its favourable subset.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) treats unordered sum classes as equally likely. (B) retains triples whose minimum is above 2. (C) omits one of the two favourable partition types.

syllabus_anchor: Binomial theorem: general term; greatest term; signed expansion
reasoning_focus: Successive absolute-term ratios locate a tied maximum before alternating signs are restored
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Expand (1−2x)^8 and then set x=1/4. Label terms by r=0,...,8, where term r contains x^r. What are the indices of the two greatest-magnitude terms, and their signed sum after substitution?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Compare successive absolute values before restoring signs.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) chooses the wrong adjacent maximum and ignores signs. (C) adds magnitudes instead of signed terms. (D) stops before the ratio reaches unity.

syllabus_anchor: Sequences and series: arithmetic progression; finite sums
reasoning_focus: Alternating AP sums require a parity check before reconstructing the last term
object_constraints_and_requested_result: The arithmetic progression is 3,5,7,... . For a positive integer n, its alternating sum a1−a2+a3−...+(−1)^(n−1)an is 11. What is an?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Split the finite alternating sum by parity of n.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) reports the alternating sum itself. (B) uses one fewer progression term. (D) uses one extra term.

syllabus_anchor: Limits: rationalisation; parameter-dependent limits
reasoning_focus: A removable algebraic cancellation changes at an exceptional parameter, so two limit operations differ
object_constraints_and_requested_result: For each fixed real a define L(a)=lim as x tends to 0 of [sqrt(1+ax)−1]/[x(x−a)], taking x through points where the quotient is defined. What are L(0) and lim as a tends to 0 of L(a), respectively?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Treat the exceptional parameter before cancelling factors and taking a later limit.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) extends the nonzero-parameter result to the excluded case. (C) extends the exceptional zero numerator to nearby nonzero parameters. (D) loses the negative sign and exchanges the limits.

syllabus_anchor: Three-dimensional geometry: planes; common intersections; distance minimisation
reasoning_focus: Parameter rank loss preserves a common plane-intersection line before its nearest point is found
object_constraints_and_requested_result: The planes are x+y+z=1, x−y+z=0 and 2x+az=b. For which a,b is their common intersection a line, and what is that line's distance from the origin?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: An independent third-plane equation selects a point; an identically satisfied one preserves a line.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) omits the required constant consistency. (B) gives an independent third-plane constraint. (D) uses a nonminimal point on the correct line.

syllabus_anchor: Permutations and combinations: circular arrangements; counting with constraints
reasoning_focus: Opposite bead positions and reflection identification require two separate circular-symmetry reductions
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Six distinct beads A–F form a regular hexagonal necklace. A and B must occupy opposite vertices. Arrangements related by a rotation or a reflection of the whole necklace are identified. How many arrangements are there?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Remove rotations first, then check whether reflection pairs can have a fixed arrangement.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) retains reflections as distinct. (D) double-counts an orientation already fixed. (C) divides by reflection twice.

syllabus_anchor: Complex numbers: conjugation; modulus; Argand-plane loci
reasoning_focus: A conjugate equation factors into real-axis and unit-circle locus components
object_constraints_and_requested_result: For z nonzero, the complex number z+1/z is real. What is the complete locus of z?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: A real complex expression equals its conjugate; retain every factor when solving the resulting equation.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) discards nonunit real solutions. (C) includes imaginary values whose reciprocal sum is generally nonreal. (D) includes an undefined zero and misses nonreal unit-modulus solutions.

syllabus_anchor: Differential equations: order and degree; separation; direct solution verification
reasoning_focus: A zero branch can join a translated positive branch smoothly, invalidating naive initial-value uniqueness
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Consider nonnegative continuously differentiable functions y on x≥0 satisfying (y')²=4y and y(0)=0, with a right derivative at zero. Which statement is correct?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Check each proposed branch and the join directly in the original differential equation before dividing by a vanishing factor.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) ignores every delayed departure. (C) assumes an initial zero derivative forces perpetual rest. (D) mistakes failure of one division step for failure of the equation.

syllabus_anchor: Trigonometric and inverse trigonometric functions: principal values; interval analysis
reasoning_focus: Different principal inverse ranges give an interval of equality plus one isolated endpoint
object_constraints_and_requested_result: For 0≤theta≤2pi, when is arcsin(sin theta)=arccos(cos theta), using the principal ranges [−pi/2,pi/2] and [0,pi]?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Evaluate each inverse composition in its stated principal range.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) ignores the fold after pi/2. (B) omits a whole interval and an endpoint. (D) compares negative and positive principal values.

syllabus_anchor: Work energy and power: kinetic energy; work; power; kinematics
reasoning_focus: Constant-force and constant-power braking produce different initial-speed distance scalings
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A particle of mass m is stopped from speed v0 by either a constant opposing force F or an opposing agency removing kinetic energy at constant power P. Ignore other forces and use the ideal models until rest. If v0 doubles, by what factors do the two stopping distances increase, respectively?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Constant-force work equals kinetic-energy loss; constant removed power is the time rate of that loss.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) assumes distance scales linearly with speed. (B) applies constant-force scaling to both. (C) exchanges the two models.

syllabus_anchor: Units and measurements: dimensions; dimensional formulae; dimensional analysis and its limitations
reasoning_focus: Dimensionless exponential arguments and additive power terms constrain coefficients without proving a proposed law
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A proposed power law is P=alpha v² exp(−beta x)+gamma sqrt(a x), where x is a positive displacement, v speed and a positive acceleration. Which dimensions are required for alpha, beta and gamma, and does dimensional consistency alone establish that the law is physically correct? Use M,L,T for mass, length and time.
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: An exponential argument is dimensionless, and every term added as a power must have power dimensions.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) makes beta x dimensional and overclaims physical proof. (B) assigns the entire power dimension to alpha without removing v² and gives gamma the wrong dimension. (D) miscounts time powers and treats a necessary test as sufficient proof.

syllabus_anchor: Mechanical properties of fluids: viscosity; Stokes law; surface tension
reasoning_focus: Drop coalescence links volume conservation to different Stokes-speed and surface-energy scalings
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Eight identical spherical liquid drops of radius r coalesce into one sphere without evaporation. Surface tension and the density difference from the surrounding viscous fluid stay constant. All drops are in the Stokes regime before and after coalescence. What are the final/initial ratios for terminal speed of one drop and total surface energy of the eight-drop system?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Conserve volume; Stokes terminal speed scales as radius squared and surface energy as total area.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) uses linear-radius speed scaling. (C) reverses the surface-energy change. (D) equates combined volume factor to speed factor.

syllabus_anchor: Rotational motion: angular momentum; moment of inertia; rolling; work and energy
reasoning_focus: A sticking corner impact uses pivot angular momentum before a separate gravitational barrier check
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A solid wheel of mass m, radius R and central moment mR²/2 rolls rightward at speed v into a step of height R/2. In the brief impact it sticks without slipping to the corner shown and loses contact with the ground. Neglect gravity's impulse. It then rotates about that fixed corner without further dissipation. What minimum incoming speed just lets its centre rise above the corner to the top of the step?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Angular momentum is conserved through the impulsive contact, then mechanical energy is conserved only during the subsequent ideal pivoting stage. The minimum is the limiting just-reaching condition.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) misses impact energy loss. (C) uses the incoming rolling energy as fully available. (D) keeps only incoming rotational energy and skips the impact angular-momentum balance.

syllabus_anchor: Thermodynamics: cyclic processes; first law; ideal-gas heat capacities
reasoning_focus: Unregenerated isochoric heating changes the efficiency of a two-isotherm cycle
object_constraints_and_requested_result: One mole of monatomic ideal gas follows a quasistatic cycle: isochoric heating from (T,V) to (2T,V), isothermal expansion to (2T,2V), isochoric cooling to (T,2V), then isothermal compression to (T,V). There is no regenerator; count all positive external heat as input. What is the efficiency?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Cycle efficiency is net work divided by all positive external heat input.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) omits the unregenerated isochoric heat cost. (C) miscounts the monatomic heat capacity and hot isothermal factor. (D) ignores unavoidable rejected heat.

syllabus_anchor: Oscillations: restoring force; SHM; fluids: buoyancy
reasoning_focus: Partial immersion adds buoyant stiffness and imposes an amplitude-dependent boundary on SHM
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A vertical spring of constant 100 N m−1 supports a 2.0 kg uniform block of horizontal cross-section 0.010 m² and height 0.20 m, partly immersed in a liquid of density 1000 kg m−3. At equilibrium its submerged depth is 0.050 m. Neglect viscosity and surface tension; take g=10 m s−2. Which statement about small vertical motion is correct?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Force balance removes constant terms but not the displacement dependence of buoyancy. Once fully emerged or fully submerged, its slope changes and the single linear law fails.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) ignores buoyant stiffness and the boundary. (B) confuses equilibrium with zero restoring slope. (D) leaves out a displacement-dependent force.

syllabus_anchor: Waves: standing sound waves; closed pipes; resonance
reasoning_focus: Successive air-column spacing determines wavelength before an end correction uses the first mode
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A tube closed by water at one end has its first two resonances with a 340 Hz source at air-column lengths 0.20 m and 0.70 m, with no resonance between them. Assume one constant open-end correction e. What are sound speed and e?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: The first two closed–open resonances have effective lengths lambda/4 and 3lambda/4.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) uses quarter-wave spacing. (C) fits spacing but not the absolute first length. (D) uses full-wave spacing and an inconsistent correction.

syllabus_anchor: Electric potential and field: dipole; superposition
reasoning_focus: Equatorial dipole potential cancels while a nonzero vector field remains
object_constraints_and_requested_result: At a far-field point on an ideal electric dipole's equatorial plane, excluding infinity, which combination is correct? Take potential zero at infinity and dipole moment p nonzero.
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Add scalar charge potentials and vector field components separately.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) treats cancellation of scalars as cancellation of vectors. (B) reverses the actual cancellations. (D) assigns a direction to scalar potential and reverses the equatorial field.

syllabus_anchor: Current electricity: resistance versus temperature; electrical power; thermal balance
reasoning_focus: Temperature-dependent resistance gives opposite thermal feedback under voltage and current control
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A resistor has R=10[1+0.010 delta T] ohm, with delta T in kelvin above ambient. Heat loss is 0.10 delta T watts. Compare an ideal 12 V supply with an ideal 1.20 A supply, each held constant. Within this linear thermal model, which steady-state conclusion is correct?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: At steady temperature, electrical heating equals heat loss; use V²/R or I²R for the actual control mode.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) ignores different feedback after warming. (C) exchanges the power laws. (D) ignores the initial positive heating.

syllabus_anchor: Nuclei: radioactive decay; half-life; daughter accumulation
reasoning_focus: Initial stable daughter abundance changes the parent survival inferred from a later isotope ratio
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A sealed sample contains radioactive parent P and its stable daughter D only. Each parent decay makes one daughter, with no losses. Initially ND/NP=2; after time t the ratio is 11. What fraction of the initial parents remains, and how many parent half-lives have elapsed?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Parent plus stable daughter number is conserved, including the initial daughters.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) ignores the original daughter contribution. (C) divides the two ratios without conserving total nuclei. (A) identifies the daughter ratio with the reciprocal surviving fraction.

syllabus_anchor: Electromagnetic induction: motional emf; magnetic force; energy conservation
reasoning_focus: A translating rod in a transverse field gradient requires matching emf and force integrals
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A conducting rod from y=0 to L moves at speed v in +x along a closed rail circuit of total resistance R. The static field is Bz(y)=B0(y/L)^2 in +z. Use B0=0.60 T, L=0.50 m, v=3.0 m s−1 and R=0.30 ohm. Neglect inductance. What are the rod's emf magnitude, positive end and external force needed for steady motion?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Replacing the field by its endpoint value triples both the emf and the relevant field integral. The power check confirms the resisting force direction and energy conversion to heat.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) uses endpoint field and reverses polarity. (B) reverses both polarity and external-force direction. (C) uses endpoint field for emf and inconsistent force accounting.

syllabus_anchor: Ray optics: lens-maker formula; thin lenses in a medium
reasoning_focus: Immersion changes lens power through relative index and can reverse a convex lens's sign
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A thin symmetric biconvex glass lens has refractive index 1.50 and surface radii +20 cm and −20 cm. What are its focal lengths when immersed separately in liquids of indices 4/3 and 1.60? Use the relative-index lens-maker formula and unchanged curvatures.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) uses the air formula twice. (C) reverses both power signs. (D) mishandles the two-surface curvature factor.

syllabus_anchor: Alternating current: phasors; capacitor and resistor; power factor
reasoning_focus: Parallel RC currents add in quadrature while only the resistor consumes mean power
object_constraints_and_requested_result: An ideal resistor and capacitor are connected in parallel to a 10 V rms sinusoidal supply. The resistor current is 1.0 A rms, and the capacitor current is 1.0 A rms. What are the rms supply current and mean power drawn?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Parallel branch currents add as phasors, and real power is the cycle-averaged energy dissipation.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) adds current magnitudes and apparent powers. (B) omits the capacitor contribution to total current. (C) ignores the resistor's dissipation.

syllabus_anchor: Semiconductor electronics: energy bands; metals, semiconductors and insulators; intrinsic carriers
reasoning_focus: Intrinsic carrier equality does not require equal electron and hole transport contributions
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Samples P,Q,R are compared. P has no band gap and its resistivity rises with temperature. Q has a small gap, its carrier concentration rises strongly on heating, and electron and hole concentrations are equal; electron mobility exceeds hole mobility. R has a much larger gap and negligible carriers in the tested range. Which statement is correct?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Conductivity is the sum of electron and hole concentration–mobility contributions.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) infers donor doping from mobility alone. (C) conflates population equality with mobility equality. (D) reverses the supplied metal classification.

syllabus_anchor: Wave optics: single-slit diffraction; Fraunhofer pattern; wavelength in a medium
reasoning_focus: Medium wavelength and measured focal length can compensate in a diffraction-width comparison
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A slit of width a is imaged as a Fraunhofer diffraction pattern in a lens's back focal plane. In air, light of vacuum wavelength lambda0 and focal length f gives central width w. The whole optical region is then filled with index 1.50 liquid; the measured focal length becomes 1.50f and the slit width is unchanged. In the paraxial limit, what happens to central width?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Central diffraction width is twice focal length times wavelength in the medium divided by slit width.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) changes focal length only. (B) changes wavelength only. (D) multiplies by both factors instead of reducing wavelength.

syllabus_anchor: The living world: taxonomic categories and nomenclature; biological classification: lichens
reasoning_focus: Shared binomial genus and a lichen association describe different classification and ecological relations
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A database lists Panthera leo and Panthera tigris under the same genus, while a lichen specimen consists of a fungal partner associated with a photosynthetic partner. Which conclusion follows without confusing naming rank with the number of biological partners?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: In binomial nomenclature the first word identifies the genus and the second contributes the specific epithet. The two listed animals therefore share Panthera but have different complete species names. A lichen is an association of fungal and photosynthetic partners, not a new rank in the genus–species hierarchy. Its composite organisation cannot be inferred from, or used to redefine, the naming rules for the animals.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) treats sharing a genus as identity of species. (B) invents a relation between a lichen association and an animal genus. (C) tries to infer a kingdom distinction from specific epithets despite the common genus.

syllabus_anchor: Morphology of flowering plants: root modifications
reasoning_focus: Respiratory, prop and stilt roots distinguished by origin and environmental function
object_constraints_and_requested_result: The root-modification diagram shows P growing upward from waterlogged soil, Q descending from spreading branches into soil, and R arising from lower stem nodes obliquely into the soil. Which assignment of their principal functions is correct?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Waterlogged soil restricts gaseous exchange, and pneumatophores projecting above it provide an aerating route. Prop roots descend from branches and can support a broad crown, as in banyan. Stilt roots arise from lower stem nodes and enter the soil obliquely, as in maize or sugarcane. Their position of origin and direction are therefore relevant to function; a root projecting upward is not simply another support column.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) exchanges the gas-exchange role of P with Q's supporting geometry. (C) attributes reproductive or photosynthetic functions not supported by these root forms. (D) confuses gas exchange with direct nitrogen-gas assimilation and labels roots as cotyledons or tendrils.

syllabus_anchor: Cell the unit of life: plasma membrane; lipid bilayer; integral proteins; membrane asymmetry
reasoning_focus: Protease access and detergent rescue distinguish opposite vesicle orientations from protein resistance or membrane leakage
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A membrane protein has tags N and C. In native cells N faces the extracellular fluid and C faces the cytosol. Two preparations form sealed vesicles. External protease removes N but not C in P, and C but not N in Q. Detergent added before protease makes both tags disappear in both preparations. Protease cannot cross an intact bilayer and the tags are detected independently. Which inference uses all controls?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: P exposes N, the region facing extracellular fluid in the native cell, while protecting the cytosolic C tag. That is the native outside-out arrangement. Q instead exposes C and protects N, which fits an inside-out orientation rather than complete membrane leakage. In each preparation the previously protected tag becomes protease-sensitive after detergent disrupts the bilayer. That control separates a physical accessibility difference from an intrinsically uncleavable tag. Independent tag detection prevents disappearance of one signal from being mistaken for loss of the entire protein.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) ignores the known native topology and invents sequence differences that are unnecessary to explain the opposite access. (C) predicts access to both tags if the membrane were freely permeable, contrary to the retained protected tag. (D) contradicts the detergent-plus-protease result by treating a reversible access restriction as permanent chemical resistance.

syllabus_anchor: Respiration in plants: tricarboxylic acid cycle; respiratory electron transport
reasoning_focus: Membrane-associated succinate dehydrogenase distinguished from the separate substrate-level GTP step
object_constraints_and_requested_result: In an actively respiring mitochondrion, an enzyme converts succinate to fumarate and transfers electrons into the respiratory chain. Most other citric-acid-cycle enzymes are in the matrix. Which combination correctly identifies the exceptional enzyme location and distinguishes its role from substrate-level phosphorylation?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Succinate dehydrogenase participates in the citric acid cycle and in electron transfer associated with the inner mitochondrial membrane. It is the location exception to the mainly matrix-localised cycle enzymes. The conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinate instead couples a high-energy substrate transformation to nucleotide phosphorylation. Electron delivery to the respiratory chain and direct substrate-level phosphorylation are distinct contributions to respiration, even though both occur within the overall mitochondrial pathway.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) gives the enzyme the wrong compartment and treats one step as the source of all ATP. (B) places it in the wrong membrane and confuses it with the GTP-forming step. (D) relocates the whole cycle and denies a retained phosphorylation reaction.

syllabus_anchor: Chemical coordination and integration: hypothalamus; pituitary hormones
reasoning_focus: Hypothalamic synthesis distinguished from posterior-pituitary storage and release
object_constraints_and_requested_result: After axons connecting the hypothalamus to the posterior pituitary are cut, posterior-pituitary hormone release is greatly reduced. Which statement correctly distinguishes the normal sites of synthesis and storage/release?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Oxytocin and vasopressin are produced by hypothalamic neurosecretory neurons. Their axons carry the hormones to endings associated with the posterior pituitary, where they are stored and released into the circulation. Cutting this connection therefore disrupts the delivery/release arrangement without making the posterior pituitary the original synthesis site. The result concerns this neural pathway rather than every endocrine gland.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) assigns synthesis to the storage/release region instead of hypothalamic neurons. (C) substitutes the anterior pituitary for the neuronal source. (D) claims a direct block in a separate gland without evidence connecting it to the severed axons.

syllabus_anchor: Human reproduction: oogenesis; fertilisation and completion of meiosis II
reasoning_focus: Oocyte arrest timing and unequal cytoplasmic allocation explain one large functional gamete
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A primary oocyte is arrested in prophase I before birth. Near ovulation it completes meiosis I unequally, and the secondary oocyte arrests again until fertilisation. Which sequence correctly states the later arrest and the reason only one large functional female gamete is normally produced?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Completion of meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes while dividing the cytoplasm unequally. The secondary oocyte keeps most of that cytoplasm, whereas a small polar body receives the other chromosome set. It enters meiosis II and arrests at metaphase II; sperm entry triggers completion. This arrangement preserves cellular resources in one prospective ovum rather than distributing them among four equally large functional eggs.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) names the wrong arrest and replaces unequal cytokinesis with equal division. (B) invents replication between the two meiotic divisions and gives the wrong phase. (C) places the arrest during chromosome separation and wrongly promotes polar bodies into equivalent ova.

syllabus_anchor: Molecular basis of inheritance: RNA world; catalytic RNA
reasoning_focus: RNA information and catalysis support an RNA-world possibility without a universal modern-genome claim
object_constraints_and_requested_result: An RNA molecule in a laboratory reaction catalyses cleavage of another RNA, and its sequence is itself copied when the necessary machinery is supplied. Which inference is consistent with the RNA-world argument without exceeding this evidence?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: An RNA sequence can encode information, and some RNA molecules also catalyse reactions. Combining these properties makes RNA a plausible participant in early systems before the modern division of labour among DNA, RNA and proteins. The experiment demonstrates capabilities under supplied conditions, not the genome type of every present-day organism. It also does not reconstruct all steps by which autonomous living systems originated.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) denies DNA's established informational role without a relevant test. (C) mistakes the chemical nature of a ribozyme for a polypeptide enzyme. (D) turns a limited molecular observation into proof of an entire historical pathway.

syllabus_anchor: Human health and disease: innate cellular barriers; acquired humoral immunity; antibodies and specificity
reasoning_focus: Antibody removal and add-back distinguish specific serum blockade from unchanged broad phagocyte ingestion
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A matched assay compares ingestion by phagocytes and blockade of microbial entry into target cells. Naive phagocytes ingest microbes A and B equally well. Serum from an A-immunised donor blocks entry of A but not B without phagocytes. Removing antibodies from that serum abolishes entry blockade; adding the isolated antibodies back restores it. Washed phagocytes from the immunised donor, tested without serum, ingest A and B at the same rates as naive phagocytes. Which conclusion and prediction are supported?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Naive and donor phagocytes show the same ingestion of A and B, so these measurements do not demonstrate an A-specific change in the washed phagocytes. By contrast, the donor serum blocks only A, and loss after antibody removal followed by rescue on add-back ties that measured blockade to antibodies. The two assays measure different processes, ingestion and entry inhibition; removing one mechanism therefore need not abolish the other. Prior immunisation is relevant to the antibody specificity, but it does not justify assigning every donor-cell effect to memory.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) contradicts equal A/B ingestion and extends antibody depletion to an independently measured cellular function. (B) ignores the antigen-specific serum effect and its removal/rescue controls. (D) confuses a soluble molecular defence with skin and denies the demonstrated antibody rescue.

syllabus_anchor: Biotechnology principles and processes: isolation of genetic material
reasoning_focus: Wall-specific lysis and selective nuclease cleanup distinguish DNA isolation from target destruction
object_constraints_and_requested_result: DNA is to be isolated from bacterial, plant and fungal cells. After appropriate cell-wall treatment, all lysates contain DNA, RNA and protein. Which protocol matches the wall differences while preserving DNA?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Bacterial, plant and fungal walls have different major structural materials, so lysozyme, cellulase and chitinase are appropriate respective choices in the standard isolation context. Once cells are lysed, RNase degrades RNA and protease removes proteins while DNA is retained. Chilled ethanol can then precipitate DNA from the prepared material. A precipitation step separates molecules; it cannot reverse nuclease hydrolysis of the desired DNA.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) mismatches walls and destroys the target with DNase. (C) assigns a fungal-wall enzyme to plant cellulose and confuses RNA removal with elimination of every nucleic acid. (D) intentionally hydrolyses the target and assumes precipitation repairs it.

syllabus_anchor: Biodiversity and conservation: in situ and ex situ conservation
reasoning_focus: Native-population protection and seed banking conserve different levels of biological context
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A threatened wild plant is protected in its native forest, and seeds from several populations are also stored in a seed bank. Which interpretation correctly classifies these conservation actions?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: In situ conservation maintains organisms within their natural ecological setting, where interactions and environmental processes can continue. A seed bank holds material outside that setting and is therefore an ex situ measure. Sampling several populations can retain more genetic representation, but storage does not reproduce pollination, competition and other forest interactions. The two approaches can complement one another without being ecologically identical.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) classifies by species identity instead of conservation setting. (B) attributes a complete ecosystem to stored seeds. (C) confuses human management with the location of conservation relative to the native habitat.

syllabus_anchor: Principles of inheritance and variation: incomplete dominance; segregation
reasoning_focus: Incomplete dominance alters phenotype classes without invalidating Mendelian allele segregation
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A true-breeding red-flowered plant is crossed with a true-breeding white-flowered plant. F1 flowers are pink, and F1 selfing produces approximately one red:two pink:one white. Under a single-locus model, which conclusion separates allele segregation from the claim of complete dominance?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: The F1 heterozygote transmits either parental allele, and selfing yields the familiar homozygote:heterozygote:homozygote genotype ratio of 1:2:1. When the heterozygote is phenotypically distinct, that genotype ratio is visible directly as three flower-colour classes. A 3:1 phenotype ratio requires one allele to mask the other completely, which is not the observation here. Recovery of both parental colours in F2 is inconsistent with irreversible blending.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) ignores the reappearance of the parental phenotypes. (C) treats complete dominance as a requirement for segregation. (D) confuses one observed colour with one copy of a gene in a diploid cell.

syllabus_anchor: Locomotion and movement: skeletal muscle; red and white muscle fibres
reasoning_focus: Red and white fibre structure predicts oxygen-dependent endurance rather than an unconditional force ranking
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Two skeletal muscle preparations have equal initial force. P has abundant myoglobin, mitochondria and capillaries; Q has much less of these. During prolonged repeated stimulation with adequate oxygen delivery, then during a brief interruption of oxygen supply, which comparison is most defensible?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Myoglobin supports oxygen availability within muscle, and abundant mitochondria and capillaries favour sustained aerobic ATP production in red fibres. White fibres rely relatively more on anaerobic routes and tend to fatigue sooner during prolonged activity under suitable oxygen supply. Removing that supply limits the oxidative route, so P's advantage cannot simply be assumed to persist unchanged. Equal initial force does not establish equal energy reserves, metabolic capacity or later endurance.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) treats limited oxidative machinery as an endurance advantage under adequate oxygen. (B) denies reversible oxygen binding and release by myoglobin. (D) infers the entire fatigue time course from one initial mechanical measurement.

syllabus_anchor: Excretory products and their elimination: kidney failure; haemodialysis
reasoning_focus: Dialysis separates urea removal from useful-ion retention through both gradients and permeability
object_constraints_and_requested_result: In a dialysis model, blood and fresh dialysing fluid are separated by a membrane permeable to urea, water and small ions but impermeable to blood cells and large plasma proteins. The fluid has the same useful small-ion concentrations as blood but no urea. Pressure is balanced, and active transport is absent. Which initial net changes are expected?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Urea has a concentration difference directed from blood to initially urea-free dialysing fluid and can cross the model membrane. Matching useful small-ion concentrations avoids a comparable initial net diffusive loss of those ions. Blood cells and large plasma proteins cannot cross despite their concentration differences because the membrane excludes them. Balanced pressure also removes an imposed bulk-filtration explanation for the selective initial solute movement.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) ignores the protein permeability restriction and reverses urea movement. (B) makes an impermeant cellular component behave like a diffusible solute. (C) treats permeability alone as sufficient for a net flux, ignoring the matched ionic concentrations.

syllabus_anchor: Cell cycle and cell division: interphase; S and G2 phases; mitosis
reasoning_focus: Edges of a pulse-labelled mitotic cohort distinguish S duration from the following G2 delay
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A very short DNA-label pulse marks cells currently in S phase. In a model culture every cell has the same fixed phase durations, all are cycling, and cells at every point of S phase are represented. The first labelled cells enter mitosis 2 h after the pulse and the last labelled cells enter mitosis 7 h after it. M lasts 1 h and the full cycle 12 h. Neglect pulse duration. What are S and G1 durations?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: The earliest labelled mitoses come from cells at the end of S, whereas the latest come from cells at its beginning.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) includes G2 in S. (C) exchanges G2 with S. (D) omits G2 from the full-cycle subtraction.

syllabus_anchor: Human reproduction: lactation; chemical coordination: prolactin and oxytocin
reasoning_focus: Prolactin-supported milk synthesis distinguished from oxytocin-driven myoepithelial ejection
object_constraints_and_requested_result: After delivery, a mother's mammary glands synthesise milk, but a temporary inhibition of oxytocin release prevents effective ejection during suckling. Which interpretation separates milk production from its delivery?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Prolactin promotes milk production in the mammary glands. Oxytocin released during the suckling response promotes contraction of myoepithelial cells, which helps move the milk into the ducts for ejection. Inhibiting the second process can therefore impair delivery even when milk has already been made. An observed failure of ejection is not by itself evidence that the synthetic process failed.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) collapses distinct hormones and actions into one. (B) infers absent synthesis from a downstream delivery defect. (D) reverses the mechanical role of contraction in ejection.

syllabus_anchor: Chemical bonding: valence bond theory; orbital overlap; sigma and pi bonding
reasoning_focus: Orbital orientation distinguishes sigma, pi and symmetry-cancelled overlap
object_constraints_and_requested_result: The internuclear axis is z. The figure compares P: two pz orbitals approaching end-on; Q: two parallel px orbitals overlapping sideways; R: an s orbital facing a px orbital whose positive and negative lobes lie symmetrically on opposite sides of the z axis. Which idealised overlap assignment is correct?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: End-on pz overlap concentrates bonding overlap around the z axis and has sigma symmetry. Parallel px orbitals can overlap on the two sides of that axis, giving pi symmetry. In R, the spherical s function overlaps equally with opposite-sign px lobes, so the positive and negative contributions cancel in the ideal symmetric arrangement. Orbital proximity alone therefore does not guarantee a nonzero bonding overlap.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) exchanges end-on and sideways labels and ignores cancellation. (B) makes the lateral overlap axially symmetric and assigns an uncancelled pi interaction to s–px. (D) denies the allowed pz end-on overlap while retaining the symmetry-forbidden s–px overlap.

syllabus_anchor: Coordination compounds: optical isomerism; oxidation state; coordination number
reasoning_focus: Signed optical rotation fixes enantiomer composition independently of complex charge and ligand denticity
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A colourless solvent contains only the two optical isomers of octahedral [Co(en)3]3+. At the chosen concentration, path length and wavelength, a pure solution of one isomer rotates +60 degrees and the other −60 degrees. Rotation is additive and the mixture gives +15 degrees. En is neutral and bidentate. What are the fraction of the positive isomer, cobalt oxidation state and metal coordination number?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Signed rotations add by isomer fraction; metal charge and donor count are independent constraints.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) uses the negative fraction and counts ligands instead of donor atoms. (C) assigns cobalt +2 despite the neutral ligands. (D) treats the measured rotation as a simple fraction of +60 without including the negative contribution.

syllabus_anchor: Thermodynamics: Hess law; Gibbs energy; dissolution energetics
reasoning_focus: Endothermic ionic dissolution can have favourable Gibbs energy after the entropy term is included
object_constraints_and_requested_result: For dissolution of one mole of an ionic solid, separating its gaseous ions costs +800 kJ mol−1 and hydration of those ions releases 760 kJ mol−1. At 298 K the dissolution entropy is +150 J mol−1 K−1. Use these data for the specified standard-state comparison. Which result is correct?
